Ahri.watch: If Ahri E Charm hits you, you can take its full follow-up damage, so move with minions between you and Ahri. Ahri Q Orb of Deception also hits on its return, so keep moving outside its return path even after dodging the first hit.
Ahri.build: Have a way to interrupt or remove Ahri E Charm first. Then build magic resistance against Ahri’s magic damage, but remember that magic resistance does not reduce the true damage dealt when Ahri Q Orb of Deception returns.
Ahri.fight: It’s best to close in with Ekko E Phase Dive just after Ahri E Charm is used. Time Ekko E Phase Dive’s empowered attack to land as Ekko Q Timewinder returns to quickly trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance, gain movement speed, and get out.
Ahri.laning: Keep a minion wave between you and Ahri to avoid Ahri E Charm while clearing the wave with Ekko Q Timewinder. Don’t spam Ekko Q Timewinder and run short on mana for a fight; save enough to use when Ahri E Charm is on cooldown.
Ahri.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of Ahri’s retreat path, then slow her with Ekko Q Timewinder. Use Ekko R Chronobreak to deal damage and disengage if needed.
Ahri.escape: Account for the movement speed from Ahri W Fox-Fire by placing Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead on her escape route, then close the gap with Ekko E Phase Dive.
Ahri.phase: Early on, avoid Ahri E Charm from behind minions and look for the right chance to fight. The available information is not enough to determine which champion is stronger in the early, mid, or late game.
Ahri.teamfight: After your team starts a fight, wait for Ahri E Charm and other crowd control to be used before entering the enemy backline. Before you go in, note a safe return position for Ekko R Chronobreak, and place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead on Ahri’s escape route.

Akali.watch: Once marked, the second dash will follow you even if you escape with Ekko E Phase Dive.
Akali.build: Akali has relatively high magic resistance, so prioritize magic penetration. Build magic resistance against her damage and get enough health to avoid easily entering the execute range of Akali R Perfect Execution.
Akali.fight: Throw Ekko Q Timewinder at Akali when she briefly appears as she enters the smoke, land your third passive hit, then use the movement speed to get out.
Akali.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of Akali’s escape route, then slow her with Ekko Q Timewinder. Use Ekko R Chronobreak only when needed.
Akali.escape: Especially before Akali R Perfect Execution comes back up, close the gap with Ekko E Phase Dive while Akali Q Five Point Strike’s slow is also down, then block her retreat with Ekko W Parallel Convergence.
Akali.phase: When you aren’t in a position to start a team fight, clear waves with Ekko Q Timewinder and apply pressure from the side lane.
Akali.teamfight: After Akali’s engage and crowd control are used and your team starts a fight, enter the enemy backline. Before going in, set a safe return point for Ekko R Chronobreak and place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead on Akali’s escape route. If you’re in danger, use Ekko R Chronobreak’s damage immunity and healing to get out.

Akshan.watch: Each time Akshan Q Avengerang hits an enemy, its range increases, so dodge both its outgoing and return paths even from behind minions. Akshan E Heroic Swing uses walls to engage or escape, so be careful when fighting near walls. If Akshan R Comeuppance targets you, the lower your health, the more dangerous it is; move behind terrain to block the bullets.
Akshan.build: Buy armor items first to mitigate damage from Akshan Q Avengerang, Akshan E Heroic Swing, and Akshan R Comeuppance. Akshan P Dirty Fighting deals two types of damage, so armor alone cannot block all of it.
Akshan.fight: Make Akshan use Akshan E Heroic Swing, then close the gap with Ekko E Phase Dive. Time Ekko E Phase Dive’s empowered attack to hit as Ekko Q Timewinder returns, triggering Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance; then use the movement speed you gain to get out.
Akshan.laning: Don’t rely on standing behind a minion wave to dodge the boomerang; watch both its outgoing and return paths. Keep vision around the river and jungle walls to spot Akshan W Going Rogue’s camouflaged roams.
Akshan.combo: When Akshan E Heroic Swing is down, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead on his escape route. Slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then use Ekko E Phase Dive to enter the field, stun him, and land an empowered attack. If Ekko Q Timewinder returns and hits again, you can follow up with Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance’s third hit.
Akshan.escape: Right after Akshan uses Akshan E Heroic Swing is your window to engage with Ekko E Phase Dive. Placing Ekko W Parallel Convergence on his escape route beforehand makes it harder for him to get away. Push Akshan into an open area without walls so he can’t use Akshan E Heroic Swing to engage or escape.
Akshan.phase: In the mid-to-late game, as your ability power stacks, Ekko’s damage, Ekko W Parallel Convergence’s shield, and Ekko R Chronobreak’s healing all become stronger. Use that strength to pressure side lanes and look for chances to fight.
Akshan.teamfight: If Akshan W Going Rogue marks you as a Scoundrel, avoid facing Akshan alone or getting within range for him to finish you off. After your team starts a fight and the enemy’s engage and crowd control are used, enter the enemy backline with a safe return position for Ekko R Chronobreak in mind. If Akshan R Comeuppance targets a low-health ally, terrain or an ally in front can block the bullets.

Ambessa.watch: When you see the windup for Ambessa W Repudiation, stop attacking and move out of its range. If you’re hit by the slow from Ambessa E Lacerate, immediately use Ekko E Phase Dive to get away and dodge the follow-up hit from Ambessa Q Cunning Sweep / Sundering Slam. Ambessa R Public Execution cannot be interrupted with crowd control, so when facing off, don’t let Ambessa and your team’s back line stand in a straight line.
Ambessa.build: Ambessa’s main damage is physical, so prioritize armor. Ambessa Q Cunning Sweep / Sundering Slam deals damage based on maximum health, so avoid relying on stacking health alone. Consider Mercury’s Treads if the enemy team has a lot of strong crowd control.
Ambessa.laning: Ambessa can close the gap with each ability, so don’t stay in front of her for long even at what seems like a safe distance while her abilities are ready. When engaging, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead along Ambessa’s path.
Ambessa.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead along Ambessa’s path, slow her with Ekko Q Timewinder, then use Ekko E Phase Dive to enter the field and stun her. Follow with an empowered attack to aim for Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance’s third hit. If you see the windup for Ambessa W Repudiation, stop attacking and move out of range, then look for another opening.
Ambessa.phase: Ambessa is strong in the mid game as core items come online, so choose an opening when she has used her abilities. In the mid-to-late game, as Ekko’s ability power stacks, his damage, Ekko W Parallel Convergence’s shield, and Ekko R Chronobreak’s healing all become stronger.
Ambessa.teamfight: Don’t engage first; enter the enemy backline after Ambessa’s engage and crowd control are used. Set a safe return point for Ekko R Chronobreak before going in, and place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead along Ambessa’s path. When facing off, don’t stand in a straight line that lets Ambessa R Public Execution hit your team’s back line.
Ambessa.escape: Go in right after Ambessa spends all her abilities and charges of Ambessa P Drakehound's Step, and Ambessa E Lacerate’s slow is down. Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence first, then close in with Ekko E Phase Dive. Before going in, decide where you want to return to with Ekko R Chronobreak.
Ambessa.fight: Engage Ambessa right after she spends her abilities and the charges of Ambessa P Drakehound's Step. Don’t damage her during Ambessa W Repudiation’s windup; after it ends, use Ekko Q Timewinder and Ekko E Phase Dive to aim for the third hit of your passive. If it’s hard to fully dodge Ambessa Q Cunning Sweep / Sundering Slam, move closer to Ambessa rather than staying near the edge of its hitbox.

Amumu.watch: If Amumu Q Bandage Toss hits you, it stuns you and lets Amumu close the gap, so dodge behind minions or jungle monsters. Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy stuns nearby enemies, so keep your distance before Amumu engages and avoid grouping with allies. The closer you are to Amumu, the more Amumu W Despair continues to deal damage based on maximum health, so don’t stay close for long.
Amumu.build: If Amumu Q Bandage Toss and Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy catch you, you may die before you can use Ekko R Chronobreak, so consider Mercury’s Treads first. Build magic resistance against Amumu’s magic damage, and avoid choosing health alone because of Amumu W Despair.
Amumu.fight: Engage with Ekko E Phase Dive after Amumu Q Bandage Toss or Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy is down. Trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance with the outbound and return hits of Ekko Q Timewinder and the empowered attack from Ekko E Phase Dive, then use the movement speed to create distance.
Amumu.laning: In lane, move unpredictably behind minions to reduce Amumu Q Bandage Toss’s gank angle.
Amumu.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of Amumu’s path. Slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then use Ekko E Phase Dive to enter the zone, stun him, and land an empowered attack. Before engaging, keep in mind where Ekko R Chronobreak will return you.
Amumu.escape: The window after Amumu Q Bandage Toss and Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy are down is your chance to engage with Ekko E Phase Dive. Amumu has no skill that lets him create distance on his own, so place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of time to catch him. If Amumu still has crowd control available, delay your engage because you could be caught before you can use Ekko R Chronobreak.
Amumu.phase: Ekko can start fights frequently once he has Ekko R Chronobreak, and he is strong in the mid to late game as he builds ability power.
Amumu.teamfight: If Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy is available, spread out from your allies and keep your distance in open terrain. After Amumu uses his engage and crowd control, if your allies start a fight, choose a safe return position first, then use Ekko E Phase Dive to reach the back line. Use Ekko R Chronobreak to deal damage and get out, judging when to cast it before you are caught by crowd control.

Anivia.watch: Anivia Q Flash Frost can explode while in flight and stun you, so don’t just sidestep slightly; use Ekko E Phase Dive to get beyond the blast radius. If Anivia Q Flash Frost hits you or you are inside a fully formed Anivia R Glacial Storm, Anivia E Frostbite deals more damage, so leave the storm immediately. In narrow paths, Anivia W Crystallize can block your escape route.
Anivia.build: Anivia’s main damage is magic damage, so build magic resistance first. If you are caught by Anivia Q Flash Frost’s stun, you could be in danger before you can use Ekko R Chronobreak, so get Mercury’s Treads.
Anivia.fight: After Anivia Q Flash Frost is down, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of her escape route and use Ekko E Phase Dive to close the distance. Combine the outbound and return hits of Ekko Q Timewinder with the empowered attack from Ekko E Phase Dive to trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance, then use the movement speed to get away. If Anivia P Rebirth is available, go in with an ally who can destroy the egg.
Anivia.laning: When ganking, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence behind Anivia first, slow her with Ekko Q Timewinder, then go in with Ekko E Phase Dive. Look for a kill when Anivia P Rebirth has already been used.
Anivia.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of Anivia’s path. Slow her with Ekko Q Timewinder, then use Ekko E Phase Dive as Ekko Q Timewinder returns to enter the zone and chain the stun into an empowered attack. Trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance with the outbound and return hits of Ekko Q Timewinder and a basic attack, then use Ekko R Chronobreak when needed.
Anivia.escape: Engage during the window after Anivia Q Flash Frost’s stun is down. Anivia has no mobility skill, so place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of time and close in with Ekko E Phase Dive; she will have trouble creating distance again. Avoid narrow paths where Anivia W Crystallize can block your escape, and choose where Ekko R Chronobreak will return you before you engage.
Anivia.phase: In the late game, account for the terrain control from Anivia W Crystallize, avoid fights in narrow paths, and pressure a side lane when you are not in a position to start a team fight.
Anivia.teamfight: Engage after Anivia Q Flash Frost and other crowd control are down and your allies have started the fight. Fight in an open lane instead of jungle passages where Anivia W Crystallize can easily block your escape, and save Flash in case a wall separates you from your allies. First establish a safe position to return to with Ekko R Chronobreak, then use Ekko W Parallel Convergence and Ekko E Phase Dive to target the back line.

Annie.watch: When white light swirls around Annie, Annie P Pyromania’s stun is ready, so stay out of her ability range. After being hit by the area attack from Annie R Summon: Tibbers, keep your distance from the summoned Tibbers, and don’t stay where Annie died even if you kill her.
Annie.fight: After Annie P Pyromania’s stun is down, close the distance and fight with Ekko E Phase Dive. Combine the outbound and return hits of Ekko Q Timewinder with the empowered attack from Ekko E Phase Dive to trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance, then use the movement speed to get away.
Annie.laning: Keep your distance while Annie P Pyromania’s stun is ready, and pressure her if she has just used it. Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of Annie’s escape route, slow her with Ekko Q Timewinder, then go in with Ekko E Phase Dive. Don’t use Ekko Q Timewinder too freely to clear the wave and run short on mana for a fight.
Annie.phase: Early on, avoid Annie P Pyromania’s stun and trade when she leaves an opening. When you are not in a position to start a team fight, clear the wave with Ekko Q Timewinder and pressure a side lane.
Annie.build: Prioritize Mercury's Treads because Annie's P Pyromania stun can keep you locked down long enough to die before you can cast Ekko R Chronobreak. Her damage is magic, so build magic resistance rather than armor to give yourself a chance to survive one combo.
Annie.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of Annie's movement. Slow her with Ekko Q Timewinder, then, as Ekko Q Timewinder returns, use Ekko E Phase Dive to enter the W sphere and stun her. Follow up with an empowered attack to trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance. Use Ekko R Chronobreak when needed, but also check whether a low-health Annie can be finished with an attack empowered by Ekko W Parallel Convergence's passive.
Annie.escape: The moment Annie's P Pyromania stun is used is your chance to engage with Ekko E Phase Dive. Annie has no mobility spell, so place Ekko W Parallel Convergence on her escape route to catch her. Before engaging, keep in mind where Ekko R Chronobreak will return you.

AurelionSol.watch: Aurelion Sol Q Breath of Light deals damage based on your maximum health and deals additional damage and grants stardust if it stays on the same target for a long time, so stand behind minions and quickly move out of its aim. When your health is low, avoid the edge of Aurelion Sol E Singularity, which can execute you, and move out immediately if you are caught. After Aurelion Sol R Falling Star / The Skies Descend is empowered, spread out from your allies to avoid the area knockup and shockwave.
AurelionSol.build: Aurelion Sol’s main damage is magic damage, so build magic resistance first. If the enemy team has a lot of strong crowd control, get Mercury’s Treads to reduce the chance of Ekko being caught and unable to use Ekko R Chronobreak.
AurelionSol.fight: Engage with Ekko E Phase Dive right after Aurelion Sol W Astral Flight is down. Trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance with the outbound and return hits of Ekko Q Timewinder and the empowered attack from Ekko E Phase Dive, then use the movement speed to get away.
AurelionSol.laning: Pressure Aurelion Sol early, before he has much stardust, but don’t take pointless hits from Aurelion Sol Q Breath of Light and help him scale. Stand behind minions when poking, and after Aurelion Sol W Astral Flight is used, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of his escape route to create an opening to engage.
AurelionSol.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of Aurelion Sol’s escape route and slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder. Before engaging, keep in mind where Ekko R Chronobreak will return you, and use it when needed.
AurelionSol.escape: The moment after Aurelion Sol W Astral Flight is used is your window to engage. When Aurelion Sol’s crowd control is down, close in with Ekko E Phase Dive, then disengage with Ekko R Chronobreak after setting up a return position.
AurelionSol.phase: Early on, Aurelion Sol has little stardust and limited mobility, so Ekko can pressure him when Aurelion Sol W Astral Flight is down. In the mid game, you can start fights frequently once Ekko R Chronobreak is available. In the late game, Aurelion Sol’s permanent stardust scaling works against you, so fight carefully instead of relying on the same engage angle.
AurelionSol.teamfight: Rather than going in first, wait until Aurelion Sol's engage and crowd control are down and your team starts the fight, then dive into the enemy backline. Before going in, set a safe return point for Ekko R Chronobreak, and spread out so several of you aren't hit together by empowered Aurelion Sol R Falling Star / The Skies Descend.

Azir.watch: Don’t stand for long in a straight line with soldiers summoned by Azir W Arise!. After Azir moves them with Azir Q Conquering Sands, approach from the side while they pause. Azir R Emperor’s Divide can knock an engaging Ekko back, so check whether Azir has used it before going in, especially in narrow passages.
Azir.build: Ekko’s magic damage is effective against Azir, so build ability power items first. To withstand Azir’s magic damage, prioritize magic resistance over armor.
Azir.fight: Go in for a short trade when Azir’s soldiers are stationary or Azir E Shifting Sands is down. Slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then use Ekko E Phase Dive to pass beside a soldier and stick to Azir. Use the movement speed from Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance to get out.
Azir.laning: When Azir safely farms with his soldiers, wait for their duration to end or for a window when he spends mana.
Azir.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of Azir’s direction of travel, then slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder and enter the sphere with Ekko E Phase Dive to stun him. As Ekko Q Timewinder returns, land Ekko E Phase Dive’s empowered attack to trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance quickly. If needed, deal damage and get out with Ekko R Chronobreak.
Azir.phase: Ekko can often start fights once Ekko R Chronobreak is available, and his damage, shield, and healing all become stronger in the mid to late game as he builds ability power. Azir also gets stronger as the game goes on, so in the late game, avoid fighting in front of his soldiers for long and go in for short trades.
Azir.teamfight: Don’t all enter through a narrow passage at once, where Azir R Emperor’s Divide could knock several of you back together. After an ally starts the fight and Azir’s knockback is down, enter the backline with Ekko W Parallel Convergence and Ekko E Phase Dive, keeping a safe return point in mind. After going in, you can deal damage and get out with Ekko R Chronobreak.
Azir.escape: Right after you make Azir use Azir E Shifting Sands is your chance to close the gap with Ekko E Phase Dive. If Azir R Emperor's Divide is also down, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence on his escape route and go in. You can block his path in advance if he tries to escape to a soldier beyond a wall.

Aurora.watch: Aurora Q Twofold Hex deals damage again when recalled, and that damage increases as the target’s health gets lower. If you’re cursed, move out of the line connecting you to Aurora, and if your health is borderline, back off before the recall. After Aurora R Between Worlds creates its zone, you’re slowed when leaving it, so decide whether to escape before the zone appears or fight inside it.
Aurora.build: Aurora P Spirit Abjuration, Aurora Q Twofold Hex, and Aurora E The Weirding all deal magic damage, so prioritize magic resistance. Aurora P Spirit Abjuration deals damage based on your maximum health, so consider magic resistance and movement speed to move out of the telegraphed area instead of simply stacking health.
Aurora.fight: Use Ekko E Phase Dive to get on Aurora and make her use Aurora E The Weirding, then re-engage immediately once she has also used Aurora W Across the Veil. Trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance with Ekko Q Timewinder’s hits on the way out and back, plus Ekko E Phase Dive’s empowered attack, then use the movement speed to get away. Avoid trading at low health while waiting for Aurora Q Twofold Hex to be recalled.
Aurora.laning: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence along Aurora’s escape route first, slow her with Ekko Q Timewinder, then enter the sphere with Ekko E Phase Dive. Ekko W Parallel Convergence has a visible tell and a windup, so don’t use it after you’re already on her. If it’s hard to start a fight, clear the wave with Ekko Q Timewinder, but don’t spam it and run out of mana for a fight.
Aurora.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence where Aurora is headed, then throw Ekko Q Timewinder. If needed, deal damage and get out with Ekko R Chronobreak.
Aurora.escape: If Aurora has only used Aurora W Across the Veil, she can still escape with Aurora E The Weirding or Aurora R Between Worlds, so check her remaining mobility. When both Aurora E The Weirding and Aurora W Across the Veil are down and she has no takedown participation, go in with Ekko E Phase Dive and look for a stun with Ekko W Parallel Convergence.
Aurora.phase: Ekko’s jungle clear is not especially fast early on, so look for ganks that make use of Ekko W Parallel Convergence’s stun. The information provided is not enough to determine which champion has the overall advantage early.
Aurora.teamfight: Don’t go in first. Wait until Aurora’s engage and crowd control are down and an ally starts the fight, then enter the backline. Before going in, keep a safe return point in mind for Ekko R Chronobreak. If Aurora jumps in and fails to participate in a takedown, look for a chance to catch her. If an ally is killed, Aurora W Across the Veil’s cooldown resets, so don’t leave a low-health ally behind as you retreat.

Brand.build: Build magic resistance against Brand’s main damage. Brand P Blaze deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid choices that only add health. If you often get stunned by Brand Q Sear, consider Mercury’s Treads first.
Brand.fight: The moment Brand W Pillar of Flame is down is an opportunity to go in. Slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then use Ekko E Phase Dive to get close and trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance with the hits on the way out and back and the empowered attack. If you’re ablaze, dodge Brand Q Sear before going in.
Brand.laning: If you last-hit next to a burning minion, you can get hit by Brand E Conflagration’s spread, so step to the side of the wave. When ganking, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence along Brand’s escape route first, slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then go in with Ekko E Phase Dive.
Brand.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence first in the direction Brand is likely to retreat. If needed, deal damage and get out with Ekko R Chronobreak.
Brand.escape: Use Ekko E Phase Dive to close the gap when Brand W Pillar of Flame is down and you aren’t ablaze. If you are ablaze, dodge the stun from Brand Q Sear before going in. Brand has no mobility spell, so it’s hard for him to create distance once you’re on him.
Brand.phase: Ekko’s jungle clear is not especially fast early, but you can look for ganks with the stun from Ekko W Parallel Convergence. In the mid to late game, as Ekko builds ability power, his damage, the shield from Ekko W Parallel Convergence, and the healing from Ekko R Chronobreak all become stronger.
Brand.teamfight: Spread out from allies to reduce the spread of Brand E Conflagration and the bounces from Brand R Pyroclasm. After the enemy’s engage and crowd control are down and an ally starts the fight, enter behind Brand. Before going in, set up a safe return point for Ekko R Chronobreak.

Briar.watch: Briar Q Head Rush is a dash and stun that also reduces resistances, so use Ekko E Phase Dive to create distance before it hits. When Briar charges Briar E Chilling Scream, move away from the wall and look for a chance to interrupt her with the stun from Ekko W Parallel Convergence placed in advance. If you become the target of Briar R Certain Death, move toward your allies and fight back together instead of running alone.
Briar.build: Prioritize armor against Briar’s main damage. Avoiding Briar Q Head Rush, which reduces resistances, takes priority over raising your resistance stats further. If the duel goes long, consider Grievous Wounds after building resistances. Choose Mercury’s Treads if the enemy team has a lot of strong crowd control.
Briar.fight: While Briar W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack is active, she chases the nearest enemy, so fight behind your frontline and watch the direction she enters from. Once Briar’s dash is down, use Ekko Q Timewinder’s hits on the way out and back and Ekko E Phase Dive’s empowered attack to trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance, then use the movement speed to escape. Before Briar R Certain Death is ready again, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence in advance and look for a chance to go in.
Briar.laning: If you’ve pushed the lane, establish vision, and don’t stay long in the middle of the lane where there’s no vision. Briar’s reckless engage is an opportunity to counterattack, so place Ekko W Parallel Convergence along her entry path first and slow her with Ekko Q Timewinder. If you encounter her in the jungle, you can reduce her health and delay her next route even if you can’t get a takedown.
Briar.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of Briar’s direction of travel, slow her with Ekko Q Timewinder, then enter the sphere with Ekko E Phase Dive to stun her. Follow up by combining the empowered attack with Ekko Q Timewinder’s returning hit to aim for the third hit of Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance. Before going in, keep a return point in mind for Ekko R Chronobreak, and use it when needed.
Briar.escape: Don’t go in just because Briar Q Head Rush is down. Briar W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack and Briar R Certain Death are also ways for her to move, so wait until several mobility spells are down, especially before her ultimate is ready again. If you see Briar charging Briar E Chilling Scream, look for a chance to interrupt her with the stun from Ekko W Parallel Convergence placed in advance.
Briar.phase: Early on, secure vision and watch out for Briar’s high takedown participation and reckless engages. Later, counterattack her engages or pressure a side lane to draw enemies away.
Briar.teamfight: Don’t go in first. Wait until Briar’s engage and crowd control are down and an ally starts the fight, then enter the backline. If Briar uses Briar W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack to chase a backline damage dealer, have the frontline stand in her path and place Ekko W Parallel Convergence along that route in advance. Choose a safe return point for Ekko R Chronobreak before going in.

Cassiopeia.watch: If Cassiopeia Q Noxious Blast hits you, create distance until the poison wears off. If Cassiopeia E Twin Fang hits you while you are poisoned, you take damage and she heals. Ekko E Phase Dive and Ekko R Chronobreak cannot be used on Cassiopeia W Miasma, so avoid it and go around. When you see Cassiopeia R Petrifying Gaze’s animation, turn away to avoid being stunned.
Cassiopeia.build: Cassiopeia Q Noxious Blast, W Miasma, and E Twin Fang all deal magic damage, so build magic resistance first. If the enemy team has a lot of hard crowd control, choose Mercury's Treads.
Cassiopeia.fight: If Cassiopeia Q Noxious Blast hits you, don’t keep fighting; engage again after the poison wears off. When Cassiopeia W Miasma is used elsewhere, set up Ekko W Parallel Convergence in advance and engage.
Cassiopeia.laning: Repeat short trades early to build a lead. When ganking, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence along Cassiopeia’s escape route first, slow her with Ekko Q Timewinder, then go in with Ekko E Phase Dive. Using Ekko Q Timewinder too often can leave you without enough mana to fight.
Cassiopeia.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence along Cassiopeia’s path first. Then slow her with Ekko Q Timewinder, enter the sphere with Ekko E Phase Dive to stun her, and land an empowered attack. If you engage as Ekko Q Timewinder returns, its outbound and return hits plus an attack can quickly trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance.
Cassiopeia.escape: Engage when Cassiopeia W Miasma has been used elsewhere and you can avoid the stun from Cassiopeia R Petrifying Gaze. Before going in, keep in mind a safe position to return to with Ekko R Chronobreak, and escape when Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance grants its movement speed.
Cassiopeia.phase: Cassiopeia’s sustained damage is strong later, so don’t fight her head-on for long. Look for a chance to catch her with Ekko W Parallel Convergence.
Cassiopeia.teamfight: Don’t jump in first. Wait until the enemy’s engage tools and crowd control are down and your team starts the fight, then enter the enemy backline. Right after Cassiopeia W Miasma is used elsewhere, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence along her path in advance to look for a stun. Choose a safe position to return to with Ekko R Chronobreak before engaging.

Diana.watch: Diana Q Crescent Strike curves through the air and leaves a mark, so dodge sideways instead of only backing away. If you are marked, Diana E Lunar Rush may have its cooldown reset, so create distance. Keep space from your allies so Diana R Moonfall doesn’t pull several of you in together.
Diana.build: The provided information gives no specific item for the first purchase, so one cannot be specified. Build magic resistance against Diana’s damage and get enough movement speed to leave the telegraphed area.
Diana.fight: Start a fight after the orbs and shield from Diana W Pale Cascade disappear. If Diana goes in first with E Lunar Rush without a mark, slow her with Ekko Q Timewinder or stun her with Ekko W Parallel Convergence to counterattack. After Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance triggers, use the movement speed it grants to escape.
Diana.laning: Don’t use Ekko Q Timewinder too often on the wave and leave yourself without enough mana to fight.
Diana.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence along Diana’s escape or engage route first. Then slow her with Ekko Q Timewinder, and when the sphere is ready, go in with Ekko E Phase Dive to stun her and land an empowered attack. Look to trigger the third hit of Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance with Ekko Q Timewinder’s outbound and return hits and an attack.
Diana.escape: Right after you make Diana use E Lunar Rush is a chance to close the gap with Ekko E Phase Dive. Against Diana when she goes in without a mark, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence in advance to block her escape route.
Diana.phase: As your ability power builds in the mid and late game, Ekko’s damage, the shield from Ekko W Parallel Convergence, and the healing from Ekko R Chronobreak all become stronger.
Diana.teamfight: Watch Diana’s flank routes with vision, and spread out so Diana R Moonfall doesn’t pull several of you in. Ekko should not engage first; enter the enemy backline after Diana’s engage tool and crowd control are down. Choose a safe position to return to with Ekko R Chronobreak before going in.

Corki.build: Build armor first against Corki E Gatling Gun and R Missile Barrage. Corki P Hextech Munitions’ true damage cannot be reduced with resistances, so get health too. Prioritize moving out of Corki E Gatling Gun’s range over building more resistances.
Corki.fight: Don’t force an engage while Corki W Valkyrie is available. Right after Corki uses W Valkyrie, slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder and close in with Ekko E Phase Dive to look for the third hit of your passive. If Corki E Gatling Gun is active in front of you, move to the side instead of trying to endure it.
Corki.laning: Pressure Corki during his weak first five levels and disrupt his farming. When ganking, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence along his escape route first, slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then go in with Ekko E Phase Dive. If you’re escaping with your position revealed after being hit by Corki Q Phosphorus Bomb, don’t save Ekko E Phase Dive; use it to create distance.
Corki.combo: When Corki W Valkyrie is down, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence along his escape route first. Then slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, enter the sphere with Ekko E Phase Dive to stun him, and land an empowered attack. If you engage as Ekko Q Timewinder returns, its outbound and return hits plus an empowered attack can quickly trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance.
Corki.escape: Right after Corki uses W Valkyrie is a window to go in with Ekko E Phase Dive. Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence along his escape route in advance to make it harder for him to get away. Check your return position with Ekko R Chronobreak before engaging.
Corki.phase: Corki’s base stats are low during his first five levels, so disrupt his growth with pressure and ganks. Corki gets stronger as he builds items and can pressure you safely with Corki R Missile Barrage later. Ekko can start fights more often after getting Ekko R Chronobreak and is strong in the mid and late game, so use that strength to limit Corki’s time to farm comfortably.
Corki.teamfight: Approach Corki after the enemy’s engage tools and crowd control are down and your team starts the fight, rather than going in first. If Corki W Valkyrie is down, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence along his escape route and enter the backline with Ekko E Phase Dive. Choose a safe position to return to with Ekko R Chronobreak before engaging.
Corki.watch: Corki R Missile Barrage also damages targets around the first one hit, so dodge out of range instead of hiding behind minions. In particular, reposition so you don’t get hit by the third missile in quick succession. If you stay exposed to Corki E Gatling Gun from the front for too long, your armor and magic resistance will be reduced, so move to the side.

Elise.build: Build magic resistance first to withstand damage from Elise’s main abilities. If you’re concerned about being unable to use Ekko R Chronobreak after being caught by Elise E Cocoon, choose Mercury's Treads for the tenacity.
Elise.fight: Fight back after Elise E Cocoon and Elise E Rappel are both down. Trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance with Ekko Q Timewinder’s outbound and return hits and Ekko E Phase Dive’s empowered attack, then use the movement speed you gain to manage the distance.
Elise.laning: Keep ample vision early and don’t push the lane recklessly when Elise is out of sight. Stand behind minions to avoid Elise E Cocoon, and when ganking, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence along the enemy’s escape route first.
Elise.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence along Elise’s retreat route in advance, then slow her with Ekko Q Timewinder and enter the sphere with Ekko E Phase Dive to stun her. Time Ekko E Phase Dive’s empowered attack with Ekko Q Timewinder’s return to trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance, and use Ekko R Chronobreak if needed.
Elise.escape: Engage when you’ve confirmed that Elise E Cocoon and Elise E Rappel are both down. Right after you make Elise use Q Venomous Bite is also a chance to close the gap with Ekko E Phase Dive; place Ekko W Parallel Convergence along her escape route.
Elise.phase: Early on, watch for Elise looking to gain an advantage through ganks, avoid giving up kills, and stall for time.
Elise.teamfight: Enter the enemy backline after enemy crowd control, including Elise E Cocoon, and engage tools are down and your team starts the fight. Before engaging, choose a safe position to return to with Ekko R Chronobreak, and use it if needed before taking crowd control or heavy damage.
Elise.watch: When your health is high, watch out for Elise Q Neurotoxin. When your health has fallen and Elise switches to Elise R Spider Form, watch for her finishing attack and be ready to use Ekko E Phase Dive or Ekko R Chronobreak.

Evelynn.watch: When the Evelynn W Allure mark appears, Evelynn is nearby preparing to charm you, so back away before the mark matures.
Evelynn.build: Build magic resistance first to withstand magic damage from Evelynn Q Hate Spike, Evelynn E Whiplash, and similar abilities. Evelynn W Allure reduces your magic resistance, and Evelynn E Whiplash deals damage based on your maximum health, so also get movement speed to help you retreat before the mark matures instead of stacking health alone.
Evelynn.fight: Keep your distance until the Evelynn W Allure mark matures, and look for an opening after Evelynn R Last Caress is used. Trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance with both the outgoing and return hits of Ekko Q Timewinder and the empowered basic attack from Ekko E Phase Dive, then use the movement speed to escape.
Evelynn.laning: Use a Control Ward to watch for Evelynn approaching, and place regular wards beside the jungle camps where she might start a fight. If you see the Evelynn W Allure mark, alert your allies and back away. When ganking, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence on the enemy’s escape route first, slow them with Ekko Q Timewinder, then go in with Ekko E Phase Dive.
Evelynn.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of time along Evelynn’s path, slow her with Ekko Q Timewinder, then enter the field with Ekko E Phase Dive to try to stun her. Hit with Ekko E Phase Dive’s empowered basic attack as Ekko Q Timewinder returns to trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance. If needed, use Ekko R Chronobreak to deal damage and get out.
Evelynn.escape: Don’t rush in after only Evelynn E Whiplash has been used; she can still escape with Evelynn R Last Caress. Before Evelynn R Last Caress comes back up, dodge the charm from Evelynn W Allure, close the gap with Ekko E Phase Dive, and block her escape route with Ekko W Parallel Convergence.
Evelynn.phase: Ekko’s early jungle clear is not especially fast, but he can look for ganks with Ekko W Parallel Convergence. Take more fights after unlocking Ekko R Chronobreak, and make use of your stronger shield and healing in the mid to late game.
Evelynn.teamfight: Evelynn targets backline damage dealers, so keep Ekko W Parallel Convergence along her approach path in areas where your team has vision. After your team starts a fight and the enemy’s engage and crowd control are used, go in with Ekko E Phase Dive. Before engaging, set a safe return point with Ekko R Chronobreak.

Fiddlesticks.build: The information provided isn’t enough to determine exactly what to buy first. To withstand Fiddlesticks’ damage, build magic resistance rather than armor, and get movement speed to escape telegraphed areas.
Fiddlesticks.fight: While Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm is down, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence on his escape route first, slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then go in with Ekko E Phase Dive. Hit with both the outgoing and return hits of Ekko Q Timewinder and Ekko E Phase Dive’s empowered basic attack to trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance, then use the movement speed to escape.
Fiddlesticks.laning: When Fiddlesticks is out of sight, keep vision in the bushes behind the lane and don’t approach closely in areas without vision. Stun him with a pre-positioned Ekko W Parallel Convergence while he channels Fiddlesticks W Bountiful Harvest to reduce his healing and chance to recast. When ganking, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence on Fiddlesticks’ escape route first, then chain Ekko Q Timewinder into Ekko E Phase Dive.
Fiddlesticks.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of time in the direction Fiddlesticks is moving, slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then enter the field with Ekko E Phase Dive to stun him. Hit with an empowered basic attack as Ekko Q Timewinder returns to trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance. If you may use Ekko R Chronobreak, set a safe return point before engaging.
Fiddlesticks.escape: After Fiddlesticks Q Terrify and Fiddlesticks E Reap’s silence are used, close the gap with Ekko E Phase Dive and trap him with Ekko W Parallel Convergence. If Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm has landed, don’t stay in its area to fight; get out with Ekko E Phase Dive or Ekko R Chronobreak.
Fiddlesticks.phase: In mid to late game objective standoffs when Fiddlesticks is out of sight, secure vision in bushes and approach paths before moving.
Fiddlesticks.teamfight: Fiddlesticks W Bountiful Harvest, Fiddlesticks E Reap, and Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm are area-of-effect abilities, so spread out from your allies and don’t bunch up in narrow passages without vision. Ekko should enter the backline after Fiddlesticks has engaged and used his crowd control, rather than going in first. Before engaging, set a safe return point with Ekko R Chronobreak, and try to stun Fiddlesticks with a pre-placed Ekko W Parallel Convergence when he starts channeling.
Fiddlesticks.watch: Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm enters the fight after channeling, so when you see the cast, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence in advance and try to stun him. If you can't interrupt it, use Ekko E Phase Dive or Ekko R Chronobreak to get out of range. Fiddlesticks's abilities can fear you in bushes without vision, and a Scarecrow Effigy standing still could be the real Fiddlesticks, so don't approach until you've checked.

Gragas.watch: If you see Gragas Q Barrel Roll, leave its radius immediately. If Gragas E Body Slam hits you near the barrel, you’re likely to be knocked up and then hit by Gragas R Explosive Cask. When Gragas has Gragas R Explosive Cask available, don’t stand with an enemy turret or the enemy team behind you.
Gragas.build: Build magic resistance first to withstand Gragas’s main damage. Gragas W Drunken Rage deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid choosing to stack health alone.
Gragas.fight: Don’t deal burst damage while Gragas is drinking with Gragas W Drunken Rage; attack after its damage reduction ends. Once Gragas E Body Slam is used, slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder and close in with Ekko E Phase Dive. Trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance with both the outgoing and return Q hits and an empowered basic attack, then escape with the movement speed it grants.
Gragas.combo: After Gragas E Body Slam is used, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence on his escape route first. Then throw Ekko Q Timewinder, and as it returns, enter the field with Ekko E Phase Dive to stun him and land an empowered basic attack. Use both the outgoing and return hits of Ekko Q Timewinder and a basic attack to aim for the third hit of Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance.
Gragas.phase: In the early to mid game, watch out for Gragas’s burst and ability to disrupt your formation, and keep your formation during objective fights. Gragas’s sustained damage is weak in the late game, so the matchup improves if you get through the early to mid game.
Gragas.teamfight: After Gragas E Body Slam and his crowd control are used and your team starts a fight, enter the backline with Ekko E Phase Dive. Before going in, set a safe return point with Ekko R Chronobreak and pre-place Ekko W Parallel Convergence on the escape route. If Gragas E Body Slam hits you, don’t counterattack there; first get outside the radius of Gragas Q Barrel Roll.
Gragas.escape: The moment after you bait Gragas E Body Slam is your window to engage. Close the distance with Ekko E Phase Dive and place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of time to block his escape route. Gragas E Body Slam’s cooldown is greatly reduced if it hits, so don’t chase a fleeing Gragas too far.
Gragas.laning: Stay out of the area where Gragas Q Barrel Roll is placed, and keep your distance so you don’t get hit by Gragas E Body Slam nearby. Once Gragas E Body Slam is down, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence on his escape route first, then slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder before going in.

Fizz.watch: Fizz E Playful / Trickster can be used to both attack and disengage, so don’t rush to use Ekko W Parallel Convergence before Fizz has finished using it. If the fish from Fizz R Chum the Waters attaches to you, move away from your allies before the shark erupts, and watch for the follow-up engage with Fizz Q Urchin Strike.
Fizz.build: Fizz’s main damage is magic damage, so build magic resistance first. Magic resistance helps you survive this opponent’s combo more than armor does.
Fizz.fight: Immediately after Fizz E Playful / Trickster has been fully used, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence and counterattack. Fizz Q Urchin Strike may still be available, so don’t overcommit to a chase just because one mobility ability was used.
Fizz.combo: Once Fizz E Playful / Trickster has been fully used, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of time in the direction he’ll move. Slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then enter the field with Ekko E Phase Dive to stun him and trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance with both the outgoing and return Q hits and an empowered basic attack. Use Ekko R Chronobreak to deal damage and get out when needed.
Fizz.escape: The moment Fizz E Playful / Trickster goes on cooldown is Ekko’s chance to engage. Check whether Fizz Q Urchin Strike has also been used, and don’t wait too long to use Ekko R Chronobreak if the shark from Fizz R Chum the Waters is about to erupt.
Fizz.phase: In the early game, take advantage of the mana burden of Fizz E Playful / Trickster by taking short trades after he has finished using it. In the late game, choose a safe return point before engaging instead of diving in first.
Fizz.teamfight: Stand close to your allies to bait out Fizz E Playful / Trickster first, then attack together once he has finished using it. Ekko should enter the backline after the enemy’s engage and crowd control are used, and set a safe return point with Ekko R Chronobreak before engaging.
Fizz.laning: Look to trade as soon as Fizz misses a last hit with Fizz W Seastone Trident and the ability goes on cooldown. Use Ekko Q Timewinder while keeping enough mana for a fight, and place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of time along Fizz's path.

Galio.watch: When Galio charges W Shield of Durand, he takes reduced damage, so don’t commit your burst; move out of taunt range. If you see Galio E Justice Punch pull him back, dodge with Ekko E Phase Dive. Move out of the overlapping gusts from Galio Q Winds of War. When you see the landing marker for Galio R Hero's Entrance, leave the area immediately.
Galio.build: Galio’s bonus magic resistance helps both his damage and defense, so prioritize magic penetration. Build magic resistance rather than armor to withstand his damage, and don’t stack health alone because Galio Q Winds of War deals damage based on your maximum health.
Galio.fight: Stop trading while Galio charges W Shield of Durand and avoid the taunt. Once Galio E Justice Punch and Galio W Shield of Durand are down, combine both hits of Ekko Q Timewinder with the empowered attack from Ekko E Phase Dive to trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance, then use the movement speed to get out.
Galio.laning: Make Galio use his abilities to clear the wave, then push while he is low on mana to limit his chance to influence other lanes with Galio R Hero's Entrance. When watching for Galio E Justice Punch, stand near a wall to shorten the distance of his dash.
Galio.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence on Galio’s escape route first, then slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder. Use Ekko R Chronobreak if needed, but keep in mind where you’ll return before engaging.
Galio.escape: Engage after Galio E Justice Punch is down and you’ve dodged the taunt from Galio W Shield of Durand. If Galio R Hero's Entrance isn’t ready, close the gap with Ekko E Phase Dive and block his escape route with Ekko W Parallel Convergence.
Galio.phase: Take advantage of Galio’s low armor early and set up opportunities to fight by placing Ekko W Parallel Convergence in advance. If the situation isn’t right for a teamfight, push a side lane to draw Galio out.
Galio.teamfight: While Galio R Hero's Entrance is ready, don’t start a skirmish with Galio’s team in another lane. In teamfights, wait for Galio’s engage and crowd control to be used and for your team to start the fight, then enter the enemy backline. Before going in, set up a safe return point with Ekko R Chronobreak.

Graves.watch: Graves Q End of the Line detonates immediately when it hits a wall, so don’t fight with your back to a wall or in a narrow jungle passage. If you’re caught in Graves W Smoke Screen, take the shortest route out of its area, then close back in with Ekko E Phase Dive.
Graves.build: Graves deals primarily physical damage, so build armor first. Plated Steelcaps early will help in early and mid-game fights.
Graves.fight: Put a minion or ally between you and Graves to block his Graves P New Destiny basic attacks. When Graves fires two shots and reloads, go in with Ekko Q Timewinder and Ekko E Phase Dive to land a third hit as well.
Graves.laning: Push or pressure the lane early to limit Graves’s opportunity to build stacks on Graves E Quickdraw. When ganking, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence on his escape route first, slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then go in with Ekko E Phase Dive.
Graves.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence in advance along Graves’s direction of travel. Slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then use Ekko E Phase Dive to enter the sphere as Q returns, connecting the stun and an empowered attack. Use Ekko R Chronobreak for damage and escape when needed.
Graves.escape: Don’t engage just because Graves E Quickdraw is down. Wait for the window when Graves R Collateral Damage is also unavailable, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence in advance, then engage with Ekko E Phase Dive. If you’re caught in Graves W Smoke Screen, leave its area first, then close back in.
Graves.teamfight: Instead of going in first, wait for the enemy’s engage and crowd control to be used and for your team to start the fight, then enter the enemy backline. Before engaging, set up a safe return point with Ekko R Chronobreak. When facing Graves, keep a minion or ally between you, and avoid fights near walls where you could be hit by Graves Q End of the Line.
Graves.phase: Early on, Ekko can push the lane or apply pressure to slow Graves’s stacking. However, Graves also gets stronger as his stacks build, so this matchup becomes less favorable as the game goes on.

Hecarim.watch: The farther Hecarim runs with Hecarim E Devastating Charge, the more damage and knockback it deals. When he turns and starts building distance, break his line of sight or move toward your allies. Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows can fear several people at once, so spread out from your team.
Hecarim.build: Hecarim’s main damage, Hecarim Q Rampage and Hecarim E Devastating Charge, is physical, so build armor first. Keep in mind that armor won’t block the magic damage from Hecarim W Spirit of Dread and Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows.
Hecarim.fight: When a fight starts, slow Hecarim with Ekko Q Timewinder to reduce both his ability to approach and his damage.
Hecarim.laning: Don’t push the lane too hard early. When ganking, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence on Hecarim’s escape route first, slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then go in with Ekko E Phase Dive.
Hecarim.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence in advance along Hecarim’s direction of travel and slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder. If needed, use Ekko R Chronobreak to return to a point you chose in advance.
Hecarim.escape: Don’t rush in just because Hecarim E Devastating Charge is down; he can escape with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. Look for an opening before Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows comes back, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence in advance, then close the gap with Ekko E Phase Dive. Before engaging, set a safe return point with Ekko R Chronobreak.
Hecarim.phase: As you build ability power, your damage, the shield from Ekko W Parallel Convergence, and the healing from Ekko R Chronobreak all increase, so look for fights in the mid to late game.
Hecarim.teamfight: Spread out from your allies so Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows doesn’t catch several of you at once. Slow Hecarim with Ekko Q Timewinder as he engages, then aim to stun him with Ekko W Parallel Convergence placed in advance along his approach path. Wait for his engage and crowd control to be used and for your team to start the fight, then enter the enemy backline. Choose your return point with Ekko R Chronobreak in advance.

Hwei.watch: If you’re caught by Hwei E Subject: Torment’s root or forced movement, you’re likely to be hit by the follow-up attack too. If Hwei’s first ability hits you, reposition immediately to dodge the second ability and the explosion from Hwei P Signature of the Visionary. Hwei Q Subject: Disaster deals damage based on your maximum and missing health, so be especially careful when your health is low.
Hwei.build: Build magic resistance first to withstand Hwei’s damage. Since Hwei Q Subject: Disaster deals damage based on your maximum health, consider movement speed to get out of telegraphed attack areas instead of only stacking health.
Hwei.fight: The moment after Hwei uses E Subject: Torment to poke or clear the wave is your chance to engage. Slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder and close in with Ekko E Phase Dive, then aim to land Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance’s third hit with both the outgoing and return Q hits and an empowered attack. Use the movement speed it triggers to get out and look for your next opportunity.
Hwei.laning: Don’t walk straight into a path where Hwei has placed an eye; take another route or send a minion ahead to consume the eye. When ganking, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence on Hwei’s escape route first, slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then go in with Ekko E Phase Dive. Take a wide route around passages where Hwei has placed a lava pool.
Hwei.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of where Hwei is moving to give yourself time to set up. Then slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder and use Ekko E Phase Dive to enter the W sphere and aim for a stun, followed by an empowered attack. If you use E to close in as Ekko Q Timewinder returns, both Q hits and the empowered attack can quickly trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance.
Hwei.escape: Hwei has no mobility ability, so close the gap with Ekko E Phase Dive right after Hwei E Subject: Torment is down. If Subject: Torment is still available, you could be rooted or knocked back while engaging, so confirm he has used it first. Before engaging, keep in mind where you’ll return with Ekko R Chronobreak.
Hwei.phase: Ekko’s jungle clear isn’t especially fast early, but you can look for ganks with the stun from Ekko W Parallel Convergence. Don’t force your way into areas where Hwei has narrowed the space; draw the enemy out by pressuring a side lane.
Hwei.teamfight: Don’t engage first as Ekko. Wait for Hwei E Subject: Torment and the enemy’s other crowd control to be used and for your team to start the fight, then enter the enemy backline. Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence where Hwei is likely to retreat, then close in with Ekko E Phase Dive. Before engaging, set a safe return point for Ekko R Chronobreak and use it for damage and escape when needed.

Irelia.watch: Irelia Q Bladesurge can chain through low-health minions to close the distance, so back away when minions are about to die. Watch out for Irelia E Flawless Duet’s stun. If you’re trapped inside Irelia R Vanguard’s Edge, wait until the blades disappear.
Irelia.fight: Right after Irelia uses Q Bladesurge is your chance to close the distance. Set up Ekko W Parallel Convergence in advance, slow her with Ekko Q Timewinder, then go in with Ekko E Phase Dive and look for a stun. Once Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance triggers, use the movement speed to get out.
Irelia.laning: Don’t leave a low-health minion between you and Irelia, and back away when minions are about to die. If you use Ekko Q Timewinder too much to clear waves, you may not have enough mana for a fight.
Irelia.escape: Go in with Ekko E Phase Dive right after Irelia Q Bladesurge is down. It’s a good time to engage if Irelia E Flawless Duet’s stun is down too. Set up Ekko W Parallel Convergence in advance to block Irelia’s escape route, and use Ekko R Chronobreak to return if things get dangerous.
Irelia.phase: If the situation isn’t right for starting a teamfight, push the lane with Ekko Q Timewinder and pressure a side lane.
Irelia.teamfight: Irelia R Vanguard’s Edge and Irelia E Flawless Duet have a big impact in teamfights, so focus Irelia first. Instead of going in first, wait until the enemy’s engage tools and crowd control are used and your team starts the fight. Before going in, set up a safe return position with Ekko R Chronobreak.
Irelia.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of time on Irelia's engage or escape route. Slow her with Ekko Q Timewinder, then enter the sphere with Ekko E Phase Dive as Ekko Q Timewinder returns to aim for a stun and empowered basic attack. Hitting both passes of Ekko Q Timewinder and an empowered basic attack quickly triggers Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance.

Jax.watch: Don’t use Ekko E Phase Dive’s empowered attack while Jax E Counter Strike is active. The more attacks it dodges, the more damage its recast deals, and you could also get hit by its area stun, so save Ekko E Phase Dive to get out of the stun’s range. Check whether Counter Strike is still active when Jax closes in with Q Leap Strike.
Jax.build: Jax has a strong stun, but the available information isn’t enough to determine your first purchase. If the enemy team has a lot of strong crowd control, choose Mercury’s Treads. Jax’s damage is a mix of physical and magic, so be careful about building only one type of resistance.
Jax.laning: Jax has the advantage in a level 1 melee trade, so don’t force close-range trades.
Jax.combo: After Jax E Counter Strike is down and Jax has used Q Leap Strike, set up Ekko W Parallel Convergence on his path. Slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, enter the sphere with Ekko E Phase Dive and stun him, then trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance with an empowered attack. If needed, use Ekko R Chronobreak with your planned return position in mind.
Jax.escape: While Jax E Counter Strike is active, save Ekko E Phase Dive to get out of the stun’s range. The window to go back in with Ekko E Phase Dive opens right after Counter Strike ends and Jax has used Q Leap Strike. Setting up Ekko W Parallel Convergence on your approach path beforehand can catch Jax.
Jax.phase: As Ekko builds ability power, his damage, shield, and healing all increase, so look for opportunities to fight and pressure side lanes in the mid to late game.
Jax.fight: Look for a trade after Jax E Counter Strike is down. Slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then land both its outgoing and returning hits and Ekko E Phase Dive's empowered basic attack to trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance. If Counter Strike is active, stop trading basic attacks and move out of its stun range.
Jax.teamfight: If Jax uses Jax Q Leap Strike to engage and activates Jax E Counter Strike, don't group up nearby; wait for the area stun to end. Right after, use Ekko W Parallel Convergence, which you placed ahead of time on Jax's path, to aim for a stun. Rather than diving in first, Ekko should dive into the enemy backline after the enemy's engage and crowd control are down, and choose a safe spot to return to with Ekko R Chronobreak beforehand.

Ivern.watch: If Ivern Q Rootcaller hits you, Ivern’s allies can dash to you, so avoid its firing angle by keeping minions or terrain between you and Ivern. Don’t go straight in on a target affected by Ivern E Triggerseed, as you may be slowed when it detonates. If Daisy! starts attacking you, move away to avoid being knocked up by her three consecutive attacks.
Ivern.fight: Close the distance with Ekko E Phase Dive right after Ivern Q Rootcaller misses. Wait until the shield on a target affected by Ivern E Triggerseed detonates before attacking. Trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance with both passes of Ekko Q Timewinder and an empowered attack, then use the movement speed to get out.
Ivern.laning: Place vision in Ivern’s jungle early to track his path as he comes to harvest camps where he planted seeds. Don’t walk casually near a newly created area of Ivern W Brushmaker; clear vision there to remove his ambush spot. When ganking, set up Ekko W Parallel Convergence on the enemy’s escape route, slow them with Ekko Q Timewinder, then go in with Ekko E Phase Dive.
Ivern.combo: Once Ivern Q Rootcaller is down, set up Ekko W Parallel Convergence in advance in Ivern’s direction of travel. Trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance with both passes of Ekko Q Timewinder and a basic attack, then use Ekko R Chronobreak to deal damage and disengage when needed.
Ivern.escape: The window to go in opens right after Ivern Q Rootcaller misses. Decide where you’ll return to in advance, and use Ekko R Chronobreak if needed before you take crowd control or heavy damage.
Ivern.phase: In the mid to late game, as Ekko builds ability power, his damage, Ekko W Parallel Convergence’s shield, and Ekko R Chronobreak’s healing all grow stronger.
Ivern.build: Prioritizing ability power increases Ekko's damage, Ekko W Parallel Convergence's shield, and Ekko R Chronobreak's healing. If you build resistance against Ivern's damage, choose magic resistance over armor. However, when Ivern's allies follow up on the root from Ivern Q Rootcaller and the knockup from Ivern R Daisy!, consider tenacity first.
Ivern.teamfight: Dive into the enemy backline after Ivern Q Rootcaller and the enemy's key crowd control are down and your team has started the fight. Don't throw Ekko Q Timewinder at enemies behind Daisy; after Ivern E Triggerseed bursts, target the enemy who was shielded. Before engaging, choose a safe spot to return to with Ekko R Chronobreak, and don't chase far if Ivern is the only one left.

Karma.watch: If you keep getting hit by Karma Q Inner Flame, Karma P Gathering Fire lets her use Karma R Mantra more often, so move behind minions or out of range. Immediately walk out of the circle left by Karma Q Inner Flame empowered by Karma R Mantra. If Karma W Focused Resolve connects, create distance before it roots you, and keep in mind that Karma heals if it was empowered by Karma R Mantra.
Karma.build: Karma’s main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first. The available information isn’t enough to determine the purchase order for specific items, but movement speed to escape Karma W Focused Resolve’s tether and Karma Q Inner Flame’s ground effect is also important.
Karma.fight: Close the distance with Ekko E Phase Dive after Karma W Focused Resolve is down and Karma E Inspire’s shield has ended. Trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance with both passes of Ekko Q Timewinder and Ekko E Phase Dive’s empowered attack, then use the movement speed to get out. Ekko’s magic damage is effective against Karma, who tends to have low magic resistance.
Karma.laning: Stand behind minions or out of range so Karma Q Inner Flame doesn’t hit you for free. When starting a fight, set up Ekko W Parallel Convergence on Karma’s escape route, slow her with Ekko Q Timewinder, then enter the sphere with Ekko E Phase Dive. If you use Ekko Q Timewinder too much on the wave, you may not have enough mana to fight.
Karma.combo: Set up Ekko W Parallel Convergence in advance in the direction Karma is moving. Use Ekko R Chronobreak when you need extra damage or an escape, and keep your return position in mind before going in.
Karma.escape: The opportunity to go in with Ekko E Phase Dive opens after Karma W Focused Resolve is down. If Karma E Inspire or a shield empowered by Karma R Mantra is active, wait until it ends before engaging. If you go in while Karma W Focused Resolve is connected, create distance before it roots you or return with Ekko R Chronobreak.
Karma.phase: Ekko’s jungle clear isn’t especially fast early on, but you can look for ganks with the stun from Ekko W Parallel Convergence. The available information isn’t enough to determine who has an absolute advantage against Karma at each stage of the game.
Karma.teamfight: Don’t go in first while Karma W Focused Resolve is available; wait for your allies to start the fight and the enemy’s crowd control to be used. After the shield from Karma E Inspire empowered by Karma R Mantra ends, set up Ekko W Parallel Convergence behind the enemy and go in with Ekko E Phase Dive. Before engaging, establish a safe position to return to with Ekko R Chronobreak.

Kassadin.watch: Kassadin’s Kassadin Q Null Sphere shield absorbs Ekko’s magic damage, so trade while Q is on cooldown. Watch for the slow from Kassadin E Force Pulse and the engage from Kassadin R Riftwalk. Don’t stand alone within R range.
Kassadin.build: Prioritize magic resistance against Kassadin’s damage. Armor and Grievous Wounds are less effective against him. The available information does not determine a specific first item.
Kassadin.fight: Once Kassadin Q Null Sphere’s shield is down, slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then use Ekko E Phase Dive as Q returns to close the gap and trigger the third hit of Ekko’s passive.
Kassadin.laning: Using abilities excessively near Kassadin reduces Kassadin E Force Pulse’s cooldown, so clear waves from outside Kassadin’s range whenever possible.
Kassadin.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of time on Kassadin’s escape path. Slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then use Ekko E Phase Dive as Q returns to enter the W sphere and aim for a stun and the third hit of Ekko’s passive. If needed, deal damage and escape with Ekko R Chronobreak.
Kassadin.escape: Right after Kassadin R Riftwalk is used is an opportunity to close in with Ekko E Phase Dive. If Kassadin E Force Pulse is also down, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence on his escape path before engaging.
Kassadin.phase: In the mid game, you can look for fights more often once Ekko R Chronobreak is available, but look for moments when Kassadin R Riftwalk is down. In the late game, Kassadin’s backline dives are dangerous, so don’t stand alone within R range; respond alongside your allies.
Kassadin.teamfight: Enter the backline after Kassadin has used R Riftwalk to engage and the enemy’s crowd control has been used. Before going in, identify a safe spot to return to with Ekko R Chronobreak, and place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of time to aim for a stun.

Karthus.watch: Karthus Q Lay Waste deals more damage when it hits you alone, so walk out of its marked area when you see the warning and, if possible, stand with minions. Karthus W Wall of Pain slows and reduces magic resistance, so go around the wall. Because of Karthus P Death Defied, watch for Karthus Q Lay Waste and Karthus E Defile even right after killing him, and move away from his corpse. Keep enough health after a fight to survive Karthus R Requiem.
Karthus.build: First, get movement speed to dodge marked areas and Karthus W Wall of Pain. When building resistance, choose magic resistance over armor because all of Karthus’s main damage is magic.
Karthus.fight: Close the gap along a path that avoids Karthus Q Lay Waste and Karthus W Wall of Pain. Combine the hits in both directions from Ekko Q Timewinder with Ekko E Phase Dive’s empowered attack to trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance, then use the movement speed you gain to leave Karthus E Defile’s range.
Karthus.laning: While Karthus farms, watch for the warning on Karthus Q Lay Waste and walk out of it; use minion positioning so you don’t get hit alone. Early on, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence on the escape path behind Karthus, who has no mobility ability, then slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder and go in with Ekko E Phase Dive. Don’t spam Ekko Q Timewinder and run out of mana for a fight.
Karthus.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of time in Karthus’s escape direction to give it time to set up. Slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then use Ekko E Phase Dive as Q returns to enter the sphere and stun him. Trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance with an empowered attack. Use Ekko R Chronobreak to deal damage and return to a safe spot you picked in advance only when needed.
Karthus.escape: Karthus has no skill to create distance on his own, so avoid Karthus W Wall of Pain and use Ekko E Phase Dive to go in when Karthus Q Lay Waste misses. Placing Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of time on his escape path can create an opportunity to stun him after you close in.
Karthus.phase: If you miss this window, Karthus will catch up by farming quickly, so keep pressuring his growth. Ekko can look for fights more often after getting Ekko R Chronobreak, and in the mid to late game, as he builds Ability Power, his damage, the shield from Ekko W Parallel Convergence, and the healing from Ekko R Chronobreak all grow stronger.
Karthus.teamfight: Go in on Karthus after the enemy’s engage tools and crowd control are down and your allies have started the fight. Before engaging, identify a safe spot to return to with Ekko R Chronobreak. If you kill Karthus, immediately move away from his corpse to avoid Karthus Q Lay Waste and Karthus E Defile while Karthus P Death Defied is active. Clear the frontline alongside your allies before Karthus gets within Karthus E Defile range.

Kayn.watch: Dodge the straight-line hit from Kayn W Blade’s Reach. If it hits, Kayn can follow up with Kayn R Umbral Trespass, so leave room to move sideways when he’s about to use W. Kayn Q Reaping Slash deals damage based on your maximum health, so also move out of its dash path.
Kayn.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Kayn Q Reaping Slash, Kayn W Blade’s Reach, and Kayn R Umbral Trespass. Avoid choices that add a lot of health alone, given Kayn Q Reaping Slash’s damage based on maximum health. If you’re dueling a Rhaast who keeps healing, get resistance first, then build Grievous Wounds.
Kayn.fight: After dodging Kayn W Blade’s Reach, slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder and close in with Ekko E Phase Dive as Q returns. Trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance with Q’s hits in both directions and E’s empowered attack, then use the movement speed to create distance. If Kayn enters a wall with Kayn E Shadow Step, look for an opportunity to damage him with Ekko Q Timewinder or interrupt him with a stun from Ekko W Parallel Convergence that you placed in advance.
Kayn.laning: When a warning appears at the edge while Kayn is inside a wall, stop trading and retreat toward your turret. When ganking, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence on Kayn’s escape path first, slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then go in with Ekko E Phase Dive. Don’t spam Ekko Q Timewinder on the wave and run out of mana for a fight.
Kayn.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of time in the direction Kayn is likely to move. Slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then use Ekko E Phase Dive as Q returns to enter the sphere and stun him. Trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance with an empowered attack. Before engaging, decide where you’ll return to with Ekko R Chronobreak, and use it to deal damage and escape when needed.
Kayn.escape: Dodge Kayn W Blade’s Reach and look for an opening after Kayn Q Reaping Slash is down. If only Kayn Q Reaping Slash is down, he can escape with Kayn R Umbral Trespass, so especially look for a window before R is available again. Close the gap with Ekko E Phase Dive during that window and block his escape with a stun from Ekko W Parallel Convergence that you placed in advance.
Kayn.phase: Kayn is weak before transforming, so pressure his jungle route early and force objectives to delay his transformation. Avoid risky fights, since giving up an early kill speeds up Kayn’s transformation.
Kayn.teamfight: Rather than engaging first, Ekko should dive into the enemy backline after Kayn's engage and crowd control are down and your team has started the fight. Set up a safe spot to return to with Ekko R Chronobreak before engaging. If Kayn R Umbral Trespass enters an ally, prepare Ekko W Parallel Convergence around the target and aim to stun Kayn as he emerges.

Khazix.watch: Kha'Zix Q Taste Their Fear deals much more damage when you are isolated, so stay near allies or minions. If Kha'Zix approaches from out of sight, watch for the empowered basic attack and slow from Kha'Zix P Unseen Threat. If Kha'Zix disappears with Kha'Zix R Void Assault, throw Ekko Q Timewinder along his expected approach path and watch for the moment he reappears.
Khazix.build: Build armor first to withstand Kha'Zix's main ability damage. Keep in mind that the bonus damage from Kha'Zix P Unseen Threat is magic damage and cannot be blocked with armor.
Khazix.fight: Trade while staying near allies or minions to avoid the isolated damage from Kha'Zix Q Taste Their Fear. Right after Kha'Zix uses Kha'Zix E Leap to engage, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence along his expected path, slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then go in with Ekko E Phase Dive. Hit both passes of Ekko Q Timewinder and an empowered basic attack to trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance, then use the movement speed to retreat.
Khazix.escape: The moment after Kha'Zix uses Kha'Zix E Leap to engage is your chance to counterattack and go in. If Kha'Zix disappears with Kha'Zix R Void Assault, don't chase recklessly; respond when he reappears.
Khazix.phase: Early on, Kha'Zix has not evolved his first ability yet, but Ekko's early jungle clear is not especially fast either, so avoid isolated fights. Once Kha'Zix has accumulated two or more evolutions in the mid game, stop acting alone and move with allies. After unlocking Ekko R Chronobreak, Ekko can start fights more often, and in the mid to late game, as ability power builds, his damage, Ekko W Parallel Convergence's shield, and Ekko R Chronobreak's healing all become stronger.
Khazix.teamfight: Group with allies in a narrow area where you have vision to prevent the isolated damage from Kha'Zix Q Taste Their Fear. Rather than diving in first, wait until engage abilities, including Kha'Zix E Leap, have been used, then place Ekko W Parallel Convergence along the entry path and enter the enemy backline. Before engaging, choose a safe spot to return to with Ekko R Chronobreak.
Khazix.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence in Kha'Zix's path first. Then slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, and when the orb is ready, use Ekko E Phase Dive to enter it and land a stun and an empowered attack. Hit with Ekko Q Timewinder again as it returns to trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance, then use Ekko R Chronobreak to return if needed.
Khazix.laning: Stay near minions to reduce the isolated damage from Kha'Zix Q Taste Their Fear. Secure vision in bushes and watch for Kha'Zix approaching with Kha'Zix P Unseen Threat. Even when pushing a side lane, don't roam alone for long, and keep a route in mind for escaping with Ekko E Phase Dive and Ekko R Chronobreak.

Kindred.build: Build armor first to withstand the physical damage from Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and Kindred E Mounting Dread. If a long duel makes the healing from Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy and Kindred R Lamb's Respite difficult to deal with, consider grievous wounds next.
Kindred.fight: Look for an opening before Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy comes back after being used, slow Kindred with Ekko Q Timewinder, then close in with Ekko E Phase Dive. Hit both passes of Ekko Q Timewinder and Ekko E Phase Dive's empowered basic attack to trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance, then use the movement speed to retreat.
Kindred.laning: Take jungle camps marked by P Mark of the Kindred first, or secure vision nearby to slow Kindred's growth. When ganking, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence along the enemy's escape path first, slow them with Ekko Q Timewinder, then go in with Ekko E Phase Dive.
Kindred.combo: Place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead of Kindred's path and slow them with Ekko Q Timewinder. If needed, deal damage and escape with Ekko R Chronobreak.
Kindred.escape: When only Kindred Q Dance of Arrows has been used, Kindred can still escape with Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy, so don't rush your engage. Go in with Ekko E Phase Dive before Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy comes back, especially when Kindred Q Dance of Arrows has also been used, and block the escape route with Ekko W Parallel Convergence.
Kindred.phase: Kindred is vulnerable to pressure early, but Ekko's early jungle clear is not especially fast either, so slow Kindred's growth by managing vision and marked camps. You can start fights more often after learning Ekko R Chronobreak, and in the mid to late game, as ability power builds, Ekko's damage, Ekko W Parallel Convergence's shield, and Ekko R Chronobreak's healing all become stronger.
Kindred.teamfight: After an ally starts the fight and the enemy's engage abilities and crowd control have been used, go toward Kindred, and choose where to return with Ekko R Chronobreak before engaging. If Kindred activates Kindred R Lamb's Respite, enter the zone so low-health allies can survive too. Kindred can keep dodging with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows in Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy, so restrict their movement with Ekko Q Timewinder's slow and Ekko W Parallel Convergence's stun.
Kindred.watch: If Kindred E Mounting Dread is on you, don't let Kindred keep attacking; use Ekko E Phase Dive to create distance. Its damage is more dangerous at low health, so don't wait too long to use Ekko R Chronobreak. Inside the Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy zone, Kindred can frequently use Kindred Q Dance of Arrows to slip away, so don't fight there for long.

LeeSin.watch: Keep your distance before team fights so Lee Sin R Dragon's Rage doesn't kick you into your allies.
LeeSin.build: Build armor first to withstand the main damage from Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike and Lee Sin R Dragon's Rage. Lee Sin E Tempest/Cripple deals magic damage and cannot be blocked with armor; if basic attacks are a problem, reducing his attack speed can also be effective.
LeeSin.fight: Avoid direct duels with Lee Sin early. Trade when Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike misses or before it comes back, after checking whether his other mobility ability is also on cooldown. Hit both passes of Ekko Q Timewinder and Ekko E Phase Dive's empowered basic attack to trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance, then use the movement speed to retreat.
LeeSin.laning: Keep your distance from walls where you have no vision, and when ganking, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence along the enemy's escape path first. Slow them with Ekko Q Timewinder, then go into the sphere with Ekko E Phase Dive.
LeeSin.combo: After Lee Sin's mobility ability is used, place Ekko W Parallel Convergence ahead in the direction he will move. Slow him with Ekko Q Timewinder, then enter the sphere with Ekko E Phase Dive as Q returns to land the stun and an empowered basic attack. Trigger Ekko P Z-Drive Resonance with both Q hits and an empowered basic attack, and use Ekko R Chronobreak when needed.
